transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah... thank you. Um, well, I guess I came in today because... I don't know, it's just been going on for a really, really long time now. I just... I wake up, and before my eyes are even fully open, before my alarm even finishes going off, I already feel just incredibly low. 

It's hard to explain, but it’s like there’s this heavy, gray feeling just sitting right on top of me. And I work as a medical assistant, so you know, I have to get up early, put my scrubs on, and get ready to be on my feet and deal with patients all day. But before I even step foot out the door, before I even get to the clinic for my shift, that heavy grayness is already there, just weighing me down. 

And the thing is, it doesn't just go away once I get moving or, you know, have some coffee or start working. It pretty much follows me through the whole entire day. Like, every single hour, whether I'm taking someone's blood pressure or just sitting in my car on my lunch break staring at the steering wheel, it's just this constant shadow dragging behind me. I just... I don't know how to shake it off anymore, and I'm just so tired of it always being there.

Have there been any times when your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt more energetic than usual, where you didn't feel like you needed much sleep or found yourself doing things more impulsively?

No... no, definitely not. Honestly, it's kind of the exact opposite of that. I mean, it's actually almost funny you ask about not needing much sleep, because I feel like I could sleep for a hundred years and still be completely exhausted. I never, ever have moments where I feel wired or energetic. 

Like, at work, some of the other medical assistants my age, they're just bouncing around the hallways, grabbing charts, chatting up the nurses, just running on iced coffee and whatever else, and I just... I look at them and I can't even fathom having that kind of energy. I don't even remember what it feels like to be that awake. And as for doing things impulsively? I don't have the energy to be impulsive. I have to overthink and drag myself through every single little step just to get my scrubs on in the morning. I don't do anything crazy or out of the blue, I don't go on sudden trips or stay up all night doing projects or anything like that. I just go to the clinic, try to survive the shift without anyone noticing how dead I feel inside, and go home to collapse. 

I mean, maybe I get a little frustrated sometimes, but only because I'm just so tired of being tired, you know? Not like this intense, angry energy or anything. So, yeah, I've never had a time where my mood was high or I felt like I could take on the world. It's just... it's always just that same heavy, flat line, right at the bottom. I wish I had a day where I felt energetic, honestly, just to see what it feels like again, but no. Nothing like that.
Have you ever had a period in your life when you felt this way before, or is this the first time you’ve experienced these symptoms?

Well, I mean... it's not like it comes and goes, if that's what you mean. It’s just been this one, single, long, endless stretch. I actually know exactly how long it’s been, because... well, it’s been going on for about two years and two months now. 

I remember the timeline so clearly because it started right around the time everything at the clinic went completely upside down. We had this massive staffing change—like, a bunch of the senior medical assistants quit all at once, management was freaking out, and they just started throwing the rest of us wherever they needed bodies. So my schedule just started rotating all over the place. One week I’d be on the early morning shift, the next I’d be closing, sometimes doing both back-to-back... it was just total chaos. 

And I remember thinking at the time, you know, "Okay, I'm just exhausted because of the crazy hours, once they hire more people, I'll bounce back and feel like myself again." But... they did hire more people eventually. The schedule calmed down. But I never went back to normal. That heavy, gray feeling just moved in during all that chaos, two years and two months ago, and it just unpacked its bags and stayed. 

It’s honestly terrifying when I sit in my car and actually think about it, because I was only 18 when it started, just out of high school and actually excited to get some real-world medical experience, and now I'm 20 and I feel like I've spent my entire adult life just... drowning. Two years and two months is a really, really long time to feel like you're walking through wet cement every single day. I keep looking back, trying to pinpoint if there was a day where it let up, but there wasn't. Just this one, massive, endless block of time since those staffing changes. So, yeah, no prior periods of feeling like this before that... just this one that never went away.
Before this current period that started two years and two months ago, have you ever had a time when you felt persistently down or lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks?

No... no, definitely not. I mean, it’s actually kind of wild to even think about what I was like before all this started, because it feels like I’m remembering a completely different person. But no, I never had anything like that happen before. 

Like I was saying, I was 18 when this whole heavy feeling started, so before that, I was just in high school. And honestly, high school was fine. I mean, it was high school, so you have your regular, everyday teenager stress, right? Like stressing over passing my anatomy and physiology classes because I knew I needed good grades to get into the medical assistant certification program right after graduation. But even when I was stressed, I never felt *down* like this. And I definitely never lost interest in things. 

Actually, it was the exact opposite. I was so motivated back then. I remember during my senior year, I got into this vocational shadowing program where I got to go to a local urgent care every Tuesday and Thursday afternoon. And I absolutely loved it. I was so fascinated by everything. I’d stand there and watch the nurses do EKGs, or watch the PAs put on splints, and I’d go home and just talk my mom's ear off about every single little detail. I had so much interest in it. And I had a life, too, you know? I hung out with my friends, we’d go to this 24-hour diner after the football games on Friday nights and just eat fries and mess around until midnight. I was just a normal kid doing normal things. 

If I ever had a bad day back then, it was just... a bad day. Like, maybe I’d bomb a math quiz and feel kind of bummed out for the afternoon, or I'd get into a stupid argument with a friend, but I would wake up the very next morning and it would be gone. I’d be totally fine again. I never, ever had a time where a bad mood stretched out for a few days, let alone two whole weeks. The idea of being stuck in a rut for two weeks back then would have sounded crazy to me. 

It’s just so weird to look back, because that guy had energy. He cared about his future, he was excited to start working in a clinic, he liked his friends... and then, bam. Two years and two months ago, the staffing crisis happened at my job, the schedule went crazy, that gray cloud rolled in, and that old version of me just completely vanished. So, yeah... to answer your question, no. Nothing even remotely close to this ever happened before I turned 18. It was just a totally normal life before the bottom completely fell out.
